artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

apple_music.editorial_notes: Neil Finn didn’t create Crowded House’s third and most rewarding album on his own, instead co-writing this lushly adventurous set with his brother (and former Split Enz foil) Tim. Woodface follows the lead of The Beatles and Beach Boys at their most psychedelic, expanding pop music’s range with bold sonic and lyrical details. While “Fall at Your Feet” is a timeless ballad as good as any found on the band’s hit-stacked 1986 debut, Woodface’s stranger turns foretell the proliferation of dreamy, obtuse indie rock. Every song is a layer cake of mesmerising melodies.
apple_music.name: Woodface

editorialNotes.short: Brother Tim helps Neil Finn and band create a quirky, melodic pop masterpiece.

lastfm.wiki_content: “Woodface” is the third studio album by Crowded House. The album was produced by Mitchell Froom and Neil Finn and was released by Capitol Records in July 1991. It features five singles: "Chocolate Cake", "Fall at Your Feet", "It's Only Natural", "Weather with You", and "Four Seasons in One Day". Woodface was a major hit in Australia and New Zealand as well as giving the band their first top ten hit album in the UK. It was listed at No. 3 in the book 100 Best Australian Albums in October 2010. It was voted number 80 in the third edition of Colin Larkin's All Time Top 1000 Albums (2000). Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Woodface is the third studio album by Crowded House, originally released in 1991 and widely regarded as the band’s most warmly melodic and richly collaborative set. Built around the songwriting partnership of Neil Finn and his brother Tim Finn, the album blends classic pop craft, close harmonies, and a slightly more expansive sound than the band’s earlier records, while still retaining the crisp hooks and emotional directness that define Crowded House.

Featuring standout songs such as “Chocolate Cake,” “Fall at Your Feet,” “Weather with You,” and “Four Seasons in One Day,” the album became a major success in Australia and New Zealand and gave the group its first top ten album in the UK. This 2026 Burnt Orange Vinyl edition on Capitol Records/Universal International presents the original album in a collectible format, highlighting a record that has grown in stature as one of the finest and most enduring releases in the Crowded House catalog.
